originalTitle: Global Market Today: Oil falls, Asian stocks rise as Iran tensions ease
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: oil prices went down and stock prices went up because the US and Iran aren't fighting as much right now. This means that people are less worried about things getting worse, so they're investing in stocks. At the same time, the value of the US dollar went down compared to other currencies. The Federal Reserve, which helps control the US economy, will soon make a decision about interest rates, and people are waiting to see what they'll do. This decision, along with upcoming reports from big tech companies, will help determine what happens in the market next.

originalTitle: Stocks in news: IDFC Bank, Maruti Suzuki, ONGC, BoB, Adani Energy
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: Some big companies like IDFC Bank, Maruti Suzuki, and ONGC will be closely watched by investors today. This is because they have recently shared their financial results for the first quarter, and investors want to see how they did. Additionally, there have been some news developments about these companies that might affect their stock prices. As a result, their shares might go up or down today, depending on how investors react to the news and financial results. This is important because it can impact the overall stock market and investor decisions.

originalTitle: US market drag keeps Dr Reddy's, Cipla under pressure despite strong product pipeline
simplifiedContent: Two major Indian pharmaceutical companies, Dr Reddy's and Cipla, had a tough time in the last quarter due to problems in the US market. Despite having many new products coming out, their profits and operating margins decreased significantly. However, their businesses in India are still doing well, which is a positive sign. The companies are expected to grow in the future thanks to new products, such as those for obesity treatment. As a result, analysts have lowered their expectations for how well these companies will do in the coming years.

originalTitle: Japans Nikkei trades sideways as investors await earnings
simplifiedContent: The Nikkei is a major stock market index in Japan, and recently it hasn't been going up or down much - it's staying relatively steady. This is because investors are waiting to see how companies have performed, which will be revealed in their upcoming earnings reports. Investors are essentially on hold, waiting for this new information before deciding what to do with their money. As a result, the market is not seeing any big changes, which is why the Nikkei is "trading sideways". This wait-and-see approach is normal when investors are anticipating important news that could impact the market.

originalTitle: Crude oil prices fall 5% after US-Iran pause strikes; Brent crude at $91 per barrel
simplifiedContent: Crude oil prices recently dropped by 5%, which is a significant decrease. This happened because of a pause in potential military action between the US and Iran, which had previously caused oil prices to rise. As a result, the price of Brent crude oil, a type of oil used as a benchmark, fell to around $91 per barrel. This is important because it can affect the cost of gasoline and other fuels, as well as the stock prices of oil-related companies. The price even briefly fell below $90 per barrel, which is considered an important support level.

originalTitle: Raja Venkatraman recommends three stocks for 27 July
simplifiedContent: A market expert named Raja Venkatraman has chosen three stocks that he thinks are good to buy on July 27. He is sharing his opinions based on how the stocks are performing technically, which means he's looking at charts and patterns to make his predictions. Venkatraman is also explaining how he thinks people should trade these stocks, which means he's giving advice on how to buy and sell them. This information might be helpful to people who are trying to decide which stocks to invest in. By following his recommendations, investors can potentially make informed decisions about their investments.
